text: Hot take. I would say, paid is for everyone. If you look at the way each platform is doing, Google introducing AI, plus with paid taking up the first four spots, you have to scroll pretty far down to get to an organic listing.
speaker: Timothy Davis
context: Lenny asks whether performance marketing is something every company should be doing or if certain business models should focus on other growth channels like SEO, sales, or word of mouth instead. Timothy argues that the digital landscape has shifted dramatically, making paid advertising essential for virtually all businesses. He explains that organic reach has become increasingly difficult as platforms prioritize paid content, forcing companies to invest in paid channels just to maintain visibility.
text_ko: 솔직히 말하면요, 제 생각엔 유료 광고(paid)는 이제 누구나 하는 거예요. 각 플랫폼이 어떻게 돌아가는지 보면, 구글이 AI를 도입한 데다 상위 네 자리를 유료 광고가 차지하고 있어서 오가닉(organic) 노출을 보려면 꽤 아래까지 스크롤해야 해요.
text_zh: 大胆说一句：我觉得付费（paid）适合每个人。你看看各个平台现在的做法——Google 推出了人工智能（AI），而且前四个位置都被付费广告（paid）占了，想看到自然结果（organic listing）得往下翻很久。
text_es: Una opinión polémica: yo diría que la publicidad de pago (paid) es para todos. Si miras cómo se están moviendo las plataformas —Google metiendo inteligencia artificial (AI), y con los espacios pagados (paid) ocupando las cuatro primeras posiciones— tienes que bajar bastante para encontrar un resultado orgánico (organic listing).
original_text: Hot take. I would say, paid is for everyone. If you look at the way each platform is doing, Google introducing AI, plus with paid taking up the first four spots, you have to scroll pretty far down to get to an organic listing. Meta, it's almost a pay for play now.

vocabulary.definition: An organic listing refers to a webpage that appears in search engine results due to its relevance to the search query, rather than through paid advertising.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of digital marketing, businesses strive to improve their organic listings through search engine optimization (SEO) techniques to increase visibility without incurring advertising costs.
vocabulary.nuance: Organic listings are often perceived as more credible by users compared to paid advertisements, making them a valuable asset for long-term brand trust.

vocabulary.definition: Introducing AI refers to the process of integrating artificial intelligence technologies into business operations or products to enhance efficiency and decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, companies are increasingly introducing AI to automate processes, analyze data, and improve customer experiences, often leading to competitive advantages.
vocabulary.nuance: The phrase conveys a sense of innovation and forward-thinking, but may also imply challenges related to implementation and ethical considerations.

text: Instead of thinking about being on top of the page, and that's like ego marketing, I want to be number one. I want to be there all the time. It's about showing to the right person as often as possible.
speaker: Timothy Davis
context: Lenny asks Timothy about common mistakes he finds when taking over performance marketing accounts from agencies. Timothy explains that many marketers focus on vanity metrics like ranking position rather than targeting effectiveness. He describes 'ego marketing' as the misguided desire to always appear first in search results, when the real goal should be reaching qualified prospects who are likely to convert.
text_ko: 페이지 맨 위에만 올라가는 걸 목표로 하는, 이른바 에고 마케팅(ego marketing) 식 사고 대신에 저는 1위를 하고 싶어요. 항상 그 자리에 있고 싶고요. 중요한 건 적절한 사람에게 가능한 한 자주 보이는 거예요.
text_zh: 别老想着要排在搜索结果第一位，那就像是自我炫耀式的营销，什么"我要当老大，我要一直霸占榜首"。关键是要尽可能多地出现在对的人面前。
text_es: En lugar de obsesionarse con estar en la primera posición, que es como marketing de ego, "quiero ser el número uno, quiero estar ahí siempre", se trata de aparecer ante la persona correcta con la mayor frecuencia posible.
key_sentence: It's about showing to the right person as often as possible.

text: Each platform is different. The user behavior is different. Make sure you're not too hard on yourself if it doesn't work. It's okay to fail because we're either winning or we're learning.
speaker: Timothy Davis
context: Lenny asks for tips on experimenting with new advertising platforms to test for signs of life. Timothy advises that marketers should expect some experiments to fail when testing new platforms, as each has unique user behaviors and requirements. He emphasizes the importance of maintaining a learning mindset rather than expecting immediate success, explaining that failed experiments still provide valuable insights for future optimization.
text_ko: 플랫폼(platform)마다 다르고 사용자 행동(user behavior)도 달라요. 잘 안 되면 자신을 너무 몰아붙이지 마세요. 실패해도 괜찮아요, 우리는 이기고 있거나 배우고 있는 거예요.
text_zh: 每个平台都不一样，用户行为也不同。如果效果不好，别对自己太苛刻。失败没关系的，反正我们要么赢，要么学到东西。
text_es: Cada plataforma es distinta. El comportamiento de los usuarios es diferente. Asegúrate de no ser muy duro contigo mismo si no funciona. Está bien fallar porque o estamos ganando o estamos aprendiendo.
key_sentence: Don't be too hard on yourself; failing means we're winning or we're learning.

vocabulary.definition: The patterns and actions of individuals when interacting with products, services, or platforms, often analyzed to improve user experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding user behavior is essential for businesses to tailor their marketing strategies, enhance product design, and increase customer satisfaction.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a focus on empirical data and analytics, emphasizing the importance of observing actual user interactions rather than relying solely on assumptions.

vocabulary.definition: To be unsuccessful in achieving a desired goal or outcome, often leading to a reassessment of strategies or approaches.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup world, failure is often viewed as a stepping stone to success, providing valuable lessons that can inform future endeavors and innovations.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'fail' carries a negative connotation, in entrepreneurial contexts it is frequently reframed as an opportunity for growth and learning.

text: I always say, where are your users? You will have some data that will allow you to understand that say right now, you're doing really well on TikTok. Some would argue that's an emerging channel right now. Great.
speaker: Timothy Davis
context: Lenny asks about signs that indicate a company has potential for paid marketing to become most of their growth, rather than just a small percentage. Timothy explains his data-driven approach to identifying promising channels by analyzing existing user behavior patterns. He suggests looking at current traffic sources and user engagement to determine which platforms warrant increased investment, then testing similar platforms that might work with repurposed content.
text_ko: 저는 항상 '사용자들이 어디에 있나요?'라고 말해요. 어떤 데이터(data)를 보면 지금 틱톡에서 꽤 잘하고 있다는 걸 알 수 있어요. 어떤 사람들은 지금 틱톡이 신흥 채널(emerging channel)이라고 보기도 해요. 좋아요.
text_zh: 我常说，你的用户在哪儿？数据会告诉你这一点，比如现在你在抖音（TikTok）上做得很不错。有人会说那是个新兴渠道(channel)，很好。
text_es: Siempre digo: ¿dónde están tus usuarios? Vas a tener datos (data) que te permitan ver que, por ejemplo, ahora mismo te está yendo muy bien en TikTok. Algunos dirían que ahora es un canal emergente (emerging channel). Genial.
key_sentence: Identify where your users are; TikTok is an emerging channel for engagement.
original_text: I always say, where are your users? You will have some data that will allow you to understand that say right now, you're doing really well on TikTok. Some would argue that's an emerging channel right now. Great. If that's doing really well for you, maybe you take... Because that content could be used on something similar like Snap, see how that does for you.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to something that is in the process of coming into existence or becoming prominent.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'emerging' often describes new markets, trends, or technologies that are gaining traction and may present future opportunities.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a sense of novelty and potential, suggesting that while something is not yet fully established, it is on the verge of significant growth.

vocabulary.definition: To grasp the meaning, significance, or nature of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, 'understand' often refers to comprehending market dynamics, consumer behavior, or data insights that inform strategic decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a deeper level of comprehension beyond surface-level knowledge, often requiring analysis and critical thinking.

text: The number one thing I tell people all the time is use your own data, start with your own data. So take the existing customer base you have, load that up into the platform to build lookalikes. From there, you can do...
speaker: Timothy Davis
context: Lenny asks for advice on running effective 'signs of life' tests when experimenting with new advertising platforms. Timothy recommends starting with lookalike audiences based on existing customer data rather than broad targeting. Lookalike audiences use platform algorithms to find users who behave similarly to a company's current customers, with percentages indicating how closely matched the targeting is - 1% being the most similar and 10% being broader.
text_ko: 제가 사람들에게 늘 제일 먼저 하는 말은 자사 데이터부터 활용하라는 거예요. 보유한 고객 데이터를 플랫폼에 올려 유사 고객(lookalikes)을 만드세요. 거기서부터 여러 가지를 해볼 수 있어요...
text_zh: 我常跟人强调的第一点就是：先用自己的数据。把你现有的客户数据导入平台(platform)，用来做相似受众(lookalikes)。接下来你就可以……
text_es: Lo primero que siempre les digo es: usen sus propios datos; empiecen por los suyos. Tomen la base de clientes que ya tienen y súbanla a la plataforma para crear audiencias similares (lookalikes). A partir de ahí pueden...
key_sentence: Use your own data to build lookalikes; load that up into the platform.
original_text: The number one thing I tell people all the time is use your own data, start with your own data. So take the existing customer base you have, load that up into the platform to build lookalikes. From there, you can do... And I'll use Meta as the example. You can do a 1%, all the way up to a 10%.

vocabulary.definition: A framework or environment that enables the development and deployment of applications, services, or technologies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, a platform can refer to software or hardware that provides the necessary tools for developers and businesses to build and operate their products.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'platform' often suggests scalability and integration capabilities, making it essential to use in contexts where these features are highlighted.

vocabulary.definition: Currently in place or available; not new or created recently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'existing' often refers to current customers, products, or systems that are already operational and can be utilized for further development or analysis.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'existing' is neutral, it can imply a limitation in innovation or growth if overemphasized, so it should be used in contexts that appreciate both current and potential future states.

text: The biggest thing I want to focus on is what is your thought process when it comes to data? Because I can teach anyone how to do Google ads. I can teach anyone how to do Meta ads. That is not the hard part.
speaker: Timothy Davis
context: Lenny asks what type of person Timothy looks for when hiring the first performance marketing specialist. Timothy explains his philosophy around hiring data-driven people over those with specific platform experience. He references the book 'The Signal and the Noise' to illustrate how advertising platforms provide overwhelming amounts of metrics, making it crucial to hire someone who can distinguish meaningful insights from irrelevant data points.
text_ko: 제가 가장 집중하고 싶은 건 데이터(data)를 다룰 때 어떤 생각을 하는지예요. 구글 광고(Google Ads) 하는 법은 누구에게나 가르쳐줄 수 있고, 메타 광고(Meta Ads)도 마찬가지예요. 그건 어려운 부분이 아니에요.
text_zh: 我最想关注的是：你看待数据的思路是什么？因为谷歌广告(Google ads)、Meta广告(Meta ads)我都能教会任何人，这并不是难点。
text_es: Lo más importante en lo que quiero centrarme es: ¿cómo piensas a la hora de trabajar con los datos? Porque puedo enseñar a cualquiera a hacer anuncios en Google (Google Ads). Puedo enseñar a cualquiera a hacer anuncios en Meta (Meta Ads). Esa no es la parte difícil.
key_sentence: The biggest thing I want to focus on is what is your thought process when it comes to data?
original_text: The biggest thing I want to focus on is what is your thought process when it comes to data? Because I can teach anyone how to do Google ads. I can teach anyone how to do Meta ads. That is not the hard part. It is the data part that is the hard part because there is so much noise going on in those accounts.

vocabulary.definition: The mental procedure or sequence of ideas that an individual follows to arrive at a conclusion or decision.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, understanding someone's thought process can reveal their decision-making style and problem-solving approach, which is crucial for collaboration and innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often implies a deeper analysis of reasoning rather than just the outcome, making it suitable for discussions about strategy or critical thinking.

text: I'm a big believer in hiring smart people and then getting out of their way. But each week having one-on-ones with them, just spot checking things, just saying, 'Hey, I looked at this. This doesn't look right.
speaker: Timothy Davis
context: Lenny asks Timothy to explain why he consistently outperforms agencies when taking over performance marketing accounts. Timothy describes his management philosophy of empowering team members while maintaining oversight through regular check-ins. He contrasts this with agencies that often spread their attention too thin across multiple clients, preventing them from diving deep into account optimization and maintaining consistent quality control.
text_ko: 저는 유능한 사람을 뽑아 놓고는 그들이 알아서 일하게 놔두는 걸 정말 믿어요. 다만 매주 일대일 미팅(one-on-one)을 하면서 가볍게 스폿체크(spot checking)를 하고, "이거 제가 봤는데 좀 이상해 보여요"라고 말하곤 해요.
text_zh: 我很赞同招聪明人，然后放手让他们去做。不过我每周还是会和他们做一对一(one-on-ones)，顺便抽查一下，随口说一句：“我看了这个，好像不太对。”
text_es: Creo firmemente en contratar a personas inteligentes y luego darles espacio para trabajar. Pero cada semana tengo reuniones uno a uno (one-on-ones) con cada persona, hago revisiones puntuales (spot checking) y les digo: "Oye, miré esto y no me cuadra."
key_sentence: Hire smart people and get out of their way while spot checking things.
original_text: I'm a big believer in hiring smart people and then getting out of their way. But each week having one-on-ones with them, just spot checking things, just saying, 'Hey, I looked at this. This doesn't look right. What's going on there?' 'Oh yeah, I do that on this day.' 'Okay, great. Just making sure you're covered.'

vocabulary.definition: The practice of randomly reviewing or inspecting a small portion of work or data to ensure quality and compliance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, spot checking is often used to maintain standards in processes, products, or employee performance without requiring exhaustive reviews.
vocabulary.nuance: Spot checking suggests a balance between oversight and trust; however, excessive reliance on it may overlook systemic issues.
